posts.title: Silica-rich debris disks seem to be produced by high-energy impacts between Mars-sized bodies around younger stars. Silica-poor ones might be formed by smaller
posts.excerpt: Silica-rich debris disks seem to be produced by high-energy impacts between Mars-sized bodies around younger stars. Silica-poor ones might be formed by smaller scale collisions across a range of ages, which is likely why they vary in brightness. https://t.co/ZdYqnGblLF

media.alt: Extreme Debris Disks, Composition Across Time plot and corresponding timeline of the solar system. The plot’s y-axis is labeled Silica with an up arrow labeled rich and a down arrow labeled poor. X-axis is labeled Age (millions of years) and starts with 1 at the left and increases by factors of ten, ending with 1000 at right. A key at right has 3 symbols: black dot is Silica-rich disk, purple is Silica-poor disk, and orange is Protoplanetary disk. All 27 orange dots are within the first 10 million years and range in silica composition. The 8 black and 13 purple dots begin to appear around 10 million. The black dots stop around 100 million. The purple dots continue right. The timeline below has the same labels as the plot’s x-axis. A gray band before 100 marks the Moon-forming impact. A gray band before 1000 marks the Late heavy bombardment. 3 blue bands stretch from left to right: Giant planet formation, Terrestrial planet formation, and Giant planet migration/orbital instability.

media.alt: Artist’s concept of a star and its debris disk against the black background of space. The star is in the background, right of center, and depicted as a small, luminous sphere. The debris disk is a large blue ring that encircles the star. The debris disk is angled toward the viewer, so that the portion nearest to the viewer extends beyond the bottom frame of the illustration. Many dark, rocky fragments are scattered throughout the debris disk. In the foreground, toward the left, is a small planetary embryo colliding into the left side of a larger spherical object. The impact site glows bright yellow and orange and has a mottled appearance, as though chunks of both colliding bodies are breaking up and being destroyed. Orange-yellow streams of vapor extend outward from the collision area. Behind the debris disk and its star are many small stars in the background. A label in the bottom right corner reads “Artist’s Concept.”

history.title: Tycho Supernova Discovered
history.description: An early observer recorded the new star now called Tycho's supernova in Cassiopeia.

history.title: Galileo Discovers 3 Moons of Jupiter
history.description: Galileo recorded objects beside Jupiter that subsequent observations revealed were orbiting the planet.

history.title: Galileo observes Saturn's rings
history.description: Galileo's telescope showed unusual structures around Saturn, an early observation of its ring system.

history.title: Andromeda Galaxy Spotted by Telescope for the 1st Time
history.description: Simon Marius recorded an early telescopic view of Andromeda, then understood as a nebulous celestial object.

history.title: Riccioli reports Venus's ashen light
history.description: Riccioli reported a faint glow on Venus's dark side; the phenomenon remains disputed.

history.title: Christiaan Huygens Discovers Saturn's Moon Titan
history.description: Huygens used his telescope to identify Titan as a natural satellite of Saturn.

history.title: Giovanni Cassini Discovers Saturn's Moon Iapetus
history.description: Giovanni Cassini identified Iapetus as another natural satellite of Saturn.

history.title: Giovanni Cassini Discovers Saturn's Moon Rhea
history.description: Giovanni Cassini identified Rhea, another large icy satellite orbiting Saturn.

history.title: Astronomer 'Accidentally' Discovers Speed Of Light
history.description: Rømer used timing variations in Jupiter's moon eclipses to show that light travels at a finite speed.

history.title: Charles Messier Discovers The 'Whirlpool Galaxy'
history.description: Charles Messier recorded the object now known as the Whirlpool Galaxy in his deep-sky catalog.

history.title: Captain James Cook Observes An Annular Solar Eclipse
history.description: James Cook observed an annular solar eclipse during his Pacific exploration voyage.

history.title: Uranus Discovered!
history.description: Herschel observed the object later recognized as Uranus, expanding the known planetary system.

history.title: William Herschel Discovers 2 Moons of Uranus
history.description: Herschel identified Titania and Oberon, the first known natural satellites of Uranus.

history.title: William Herschel discovers Mimas
history.description: Herschel identified Mimas, one of Saturn's moons, during telescopic observations.

history.title: Giuseppe Piazzi Discovers Ceres
history.description: Piazzi identified Ceres, opening the study of the large population of small bodies between Mars and Jupiter.

history.title: Alais Meteorite Brings Organic Chemicals from Space
history.description: A carbonaceous meteorite fell near Alais in France; later study identified organic material within it.

history.title: Heinrich Olbers Discovers Asteroid Vesta
history.description: Heinrich Olbers identified Vesta, one of the largest objects in the main asteroid belt.

history.title: First Photo of the Moon

history.title: MetOp-C launches
history.description: MetOp-C began a mission for weather.

history.title: New Horizons: Arrokoth Flyby
history.description: Arrokoth Flyby.

history.title: Beresheet launches Israel's first mission to the Moon
history.description: SpaceIL and Israel Aerospace Industries sent Beresheet toward the Moon on a Falcon 9 rideshare. The privately funded lander was Israel's first lunar mission.

history.title: Beresheet becomes the first Israeli spacecraft to orbit the Moon
history.description: Beresheet completed lunar orbit insertion, making Israel a lunar-orbiting nation and demonstrating that a privately funded mission could reach orbit around the Moon.

history.title: Beresheet's historic Israeli lunar landing attempt ends in impact
history.description: Israel's Beresheet spacecraft lost contact during its descent and struck the Moon. The mission had achieved lunar orbit, but the attempt did not produce a successful soft landing.

history.title: Chandrayaan-2 launches
history.description: India launched its second lunar mission from Sriharikota.

history.title: Chandrayaan-2 enters lunar orbit
history.description: The Indian spacecraft completed its lunar orbit insertion.

history.title: OPS-SAT launches
history.description: OPS-SAT began a mission for technology demonstration. ESA's tiny, open-platform, flying test-bed demonstrating innovative technology.

history.title: Solar Orbiter launches
history.description: Solar Orbiter began a mission for science. Obtaining close-up, high-latitude observations of the Sun.

history.title: Ofeq 16 launches from Israel
history.description: Israel launched the Ofeq 16 (Ofek 16) electro-optical observation satellite aboard Shavit from Palmachim, adding a new spacecraft to its established reconnaissance satellite program.

history.title: Sentinel-6A launches
history.description: Sentinel-6A began a mission for earth observation.

history.title: Hayabusa2’s sample capsule is recovered
history.description: JAXA recovered the Hayabusa2 capsule in Australia with material collected from carbon-rich asteroid Ryugu.

history.title: Technion's Adelis-SAMSON satellite trio launches
history.description: Three Israeli nanosatellites developed by the Technion launched together from Baikonur. Adelis-SAMSON was designed to test autonomous formation flight and the location of radio-signal sources on Earth.

history.title: Israel signs the Artemis Accords
history.description: The Israel Space Agency signed the Artemis Accords in Tel Aviv, joining the framework of principles for international cooperation in civil space exploration.

history.title: Eytan Stibbe launches on Ax-1 with Israel's Rakia mission
history.description: Eytan Stibbe became the second Israeli in space aboard Axiom Mission 1, the first all-private astronaut mission to the International Space Station. His Rakia mission carried Israeli research and educational activities.

history.title: Eytan Stibbe becomes the first Israeli aboard the ISS
history.description: Crew Dragon Endeavour docked with the International Space Station carrying the Ax-1 crew. Eytan Stibbe became Israel's first visitor to the orbital laboratory.

history.title: Eytan Stibbe returns to Earth after the Rakia mission
history.description: Israel's Eytan Stibbe and his Ax-1 crewmates returned aboard Crew Dragon Endeavour, splashing down off Florida after their research visit to the International Space Station.

history.title: Artemis I launches
history.description: The first Space Launch System flight sent an uncrewed Orion spacecraft around the Moon and back.

history.title: Ofeq 13 launches Israel's next radar observation satellite
history.description: Israel launched Ofeq 13 (Ofek 13) aboard Shavit. The IAI-built satellite used synthetic-aperture radar for observation in darkness and adverse weather, continuing the country's radar satellite program.

history.title: Juice launches
history.description: Juice began a mission for science. Exploring the Jupiter system.

history.title: Euclid launches
history.description: ESA's Euclid observatory launched to map the geometry of the dark universe and investigate dark matter and dark energy.

history.title: Chandrayaan-3 launches
history.description: India launched its third lunar mission with a lander and rover.

history.title: Chandrayaan-3 lands on the Moon
history.description: India achieved its first lunar soft landing with Vikram in the Moon's southern high latitudes.

history.title: OSIRIS-REx returns asteroid samples to Earth
history.description: NASA's OSIRIS-REx capsule delivered material collected from asteroid Bennu.

history.title: Sentinel-2C launches
history.description: Sentinel-2C began a mission for earth observation. Delivering high-resolution images for Europe's Copernicus.

history.title: New Horizons passes 60 astronomical units from the Sun
history.description: New Horizons reached a distance from the Sun 60 times Earth’s average orbital distance.

history.title: Hera launches
history.description: Hera began a mission for space safety. Europe's first planetary defence mission heading to a double-asteroid system.

history.title: Sentinel-1C launches
history.description: Sentinel-1C began a mission for earth observation. Advanced radar technology to provide an all-weather, day-and-night imagery of Earth’s surface; Sentinel-1C and -1D introduce new capabilities for detecting and monitoring maritime traffic.

history.title: Biomass launches
history.description: Biomass began a mission for earth observation. P-band synthetic aperture radar to deliver new information about forests and their role in the carbon cycle.

history.title: Dror 1 launches Israel's national communications satellite
history.description: The IAI-built Dror 1 satellite launched on Falcon 9 from Cape Canaveral to support Israel's national communications needs with a flexible digital payload.

history.title: Ofeq 19 launches from Israel on Shavit
history.description: Israel launched Ofeq 19 (Ofek 19), a radar observation satellite built by IAI, from Palmachim aboard Shavit 2, extending the existing national observation satellite series.

history.title: Robert Goddard flies the first liquid-fueled rocket
history.description: Goddard's small rocket flew at Auburn, Massachusetts, proving liquid propulsion that would underpin later launch vehicles.

history.title: Sputnik 2 carries Laika into orbit
history.description: Laika became the first animal to orbit Earth, an early step toward human spaceflight.

history.title: Explorer 1 becomes the first U.S. satellite
history.description: Explorer 1 entered orbit and returned the data that led to discovery of the Van Allen radiation belts.

history.title: NASA opens for business
history.description: The National Aeronautics and Space Administration formally began operations as the United States' civilian space agency.

history.title: Luna 3 photographs the Moon's far side
history.description: Luna 3 returned humanity's first views of the lunar hemisphere that never faces Earth.

history.title: TIROS-1 begins weather observation from orbit
history.description: TIROS-1 became the first successful meteorological satellite and demonstrated weather imaging from space.

history.title: John Glenn becomes the first American to orbit Earth
history.description: Glenn completed three Earth orbits aboard Friendship 7.

history.title: Telstar 1 starts the satellite communications era
history.description: The first active communications satellite launched for a private company and soon relayed public transatlantic television.

history.title: Mariner 2 completes the first successful planetary encounter
history.description: Mariner 2 flew past Venus and became the first successful planetary science mission.

history.title: Syncom 3 pioneers geostationary communications
history.description: Syncom 3 launched before becoming the first satellite stationed in a geostationary orbit over a chosen longitude.

history.title: Alexei Leonov performs the first spacewalk
history.description: Leonov left Voskhod 2 for the first extravehicular activity in history.

history.title: Mariner 4 returns the first close views of Mars
history.description: Mariner 4 made the first successful Mars flyby and returned the first close-up images of another planet.

history.title: Gemini VI-A and Gemini VII complete the first space rendezvous
history.description: The two crewed spacecraft met and flew in formation, proving a capability essential for lunar missions and space stations.

history.title: Luna 9 makes the first soft landing on the Moon
history.description: The Soviet lander achieved the first survivable lunar landing and returned the first pictures from the surface.

history.title: Apollo 1 crew is lost in a launch-pad fire
history.description: Virgil Grissom, Edward White and Roger Chaffee died during a preflight test, prompting major spacecraft safety changes.

history.title: Soyuz 1 ends in the first fatal spaceflight accident
history.description: Cosmonaut Vladimir Komarov died when the Soyuz 1 descent module's parachute system failed during return.

history.title: Apollo 13 crew returns safely to Earth
history.description: Jim Lovell, Jack Swigert and Fred Haise splashed down safely after an oxygen-tank explosion forced NASA to abort their Moon landing.

history.title: Salyut 1 becomes the first space station
history.description: The Soviet Union placed the world's first space station into orbit.

history.title: Mariner 9 becomes the first spacecraft to orbit another planet
history.description: Mariner 9 entered orbit around Mars and later mapped most of the planet.

history.title: Mars 3 makes the first survivable landing on Mars
history.description: The Soviet lander reached the surface intact and transmitted briefly before contact was lost.

history.title: Landsat 1 begins continuous civilian Earth observation
history.description: Landsat 1 became the first satellite mission dedicated to monitoring Earth's land surfaces.

history.title: Apollo 17 makes the final crewed Moon landing of the Apollo era
history.description: Eugene Cernan and Harrison Schmitt landed in Taurus-Littrow on the sixth and most recent crewed lunar landing.

history.title: Skylab launches as the first U.S. space station
history.description: Skylab entered orbit and later hosted three astronaut crews for science and solar observations.

history.title: Aryabhata becomes India's first satellite
history.description: India's first satellite launched aboard a Soviet Kosmos-3M vehicle.

history.title: Apollo and Soyuz dock in orbit
history.description: American and Soviet crews completed the first international human-spaceflight docking and met in orbit.

history.title: Bruce McCandless makes the first untethered spacewalk
history.description: McCandless flew free of Challenger using the Manned Maneuvering Unit during STS-41B.

history.title: Mir begins a new era of long-duration space stations
history.description: The Soviet Union launched Mir's base block, beginning assembly of the first modular space station.

history.title: Atlantis completes the first Shuttle-Mir docking
history.description: STS-71 joined a U.S. space shuttle with Russia's Mir station for the first time and exchanged crew members in orbit.

history.title: Zarya launches to begin International Space Station assembly
history.description: The Russian-built Zarya module became the first element of the International Space Station in orbit.

history.title: Continuous human presence begins aboard the ISS
history.description: Expedition 1 docked with the International Space Station, beginning uninterrupted human occupation in orbit.

history.title: Shenzhou 5 carries China's first astronaut
history.description: Yang Liwei launched aboard Shenzhou 5, making China the third nation to independently send a human into orbit.

history.title: SpaceShipOne completes the first privately funded human spaceflight
history.description: Mike Melvill flew SpaceShipOne beyond the Kármán line in a landmark for commercial human spaceflight.

history.title: Falcon 1 becomes the first privately developed liquid-fueled rocket to orbit
history.description: SpaceX's fourth Falcon 1 flight reached Earth orbit, a landmark for privately financed launch vehicles.

history.title: Hayabusa returns the first asteroid samples to Earth
history.description: JAXA's Hayabusa capsule returned material from asteroid Itokawa after a seven-year mission.

history.title: Curiosity lands on Mars
history.description: NASA's Curiosity rover used the new sky-crane landing system to reach Gale Crater and begin studying ancient habitability.

history.title: Falcon 9 makes the first landing of an orbital-class booster
history.description: A Falcon 9 first stage returned to Landing Zone 1 after launch, demonstrating a central capability for orbital rocket reuse.

history.title: Gaia publishes its first star catalog
history.description: ESA released Gaia Data Release 1, the mission's first major public map of stellar positions and brightness.

history.title: Chang'e 4 makes the first soft landing on the Moon's far side
history.description: China's Chang'e 4 lander reached Von Kármán crater and returned the first close views from the lunar far side.

history.title: Crew Dragon Demo-2 opens the commercial crew era
history.description: NASA astronauts launched from U.S. soil aboard a commercially built and operated spacecraft for the first time.

history.title: Perseverance lands in Jezero crater
history.description: NASA's Perseverance rover landed on Mars to seek signs of ancient microbial life and cache samples for possible return.

history.title: Ingenuity makes the first powered flight on another planet
history.description: NASA's Ingenuity helicopter completed a powered, controlled flight above Mars.

history.title: Tianhe launches to begin China's space station
history.description: China launched the Tianhe core module, starting on-orbit construction of its modular space station.

history.title: James Webb Space Telescope launches
history.description: The NASA-ESA-CSA infrared observatory launched aboard an Ariane 5 toward the Sun-Earth L2 point.

history.title: DART demonstrates asteroid deflection
history.description: NASA's DART spacecraft deliberately struck Dimorphos and measurably changed the asteroid moonlet's orbit.

history.title: SLIM demonstrates precision lunar landing
history.description: JAXA's SLIM reached the Moon within about 55 meters of its target, demonstrating pinpoint landing technology.

history.title: Odysseus makes the first commercial uncrewed Moon landing
history.description: Intuitive Machines' Odysseus delivered NASA instruments near the lunar south pole, the first U.S. soft landing since Apollo 17.

history.title: Chang'e 6 returns the first samples from the Moon's far side
history.description: China's Chang'e 6 return capsule delivered the first lunar material ever collected from the far side.

history.title: Blue Ghost completes the first fully successful commercial Moon landing
history.description: Firefly Aerospace's Blue Ghost landed upright in Mare Crisium and began operating ten NASA science and technology payloads.

history.title: Astérix becomes France's first satellite
history.description: A French Diamant-A rocket placed Astérix into orbit, making France the third nation able to launch a satellite independently.

history.title: Gemini VIII completes the first docking in space
history.description: Neil Armstrong and David Scott docked Gemini VIII with an Agena target vehicle, proving a technique essential to later Moon missions and space stations.

history.title: Luna 10 becomes the first spacecraft to orbit the Moon
history.description: The Soviet Luna 10 probe entered lunar orbit and became the Moon's first artificial satellite.

history.title: Lunar Orbiter 1 takes the first Earth view from lunar orbit
history.description: NASA's Lunar Orbiter 1 captured the first photograph of Earth from lunar orbit while surveying lunar terrain for Apollo.

history.title: The Outer Space Treaty opens for signature
history.description: The treaty that established the basic international legal framework for activities in outer space opened for signature in London, Moscow, and Washington.

history.title: OHSUMI becomes Japan's first satellite
history.description: An L-4S rocket placed OHSUMI into orbit, opening Japan's satellite and space-science era.

history.title: Dong Fang Hong 1 becomes China's first satellite
history.description: A Long March 1 placed Dong Fang Hong 1 into orbit, making China the fifth nation to launch a satellite independently.

history.title: Luna 16 returns the first robotic lunar samples
history.description: Luna 16 delivered about 101 grams of lunar material to Earth, the first automated sample return from another world.

history.title: Lunokhod 1 begins the first rover mission on another world
history.description: Luna 17 landed in Mare Imbrium and deployed Lunokhod 1, the first robotic rover to explore a world beyond Earth.

history.title: Venera 7 returns data from the surface of Venus
history.description: The Soviet Venera 7 became the first spacecraft to land successfully on another planet and transmit data from its surface.

history.title: The Soyuz 11 crew is lost during return to Earth
history.description: Georgi Dobrovolski, Vladislav Volkov, and Viktor Patsayev died after their Soyuz depressurized, leading to major spacecraft and pressure-suit changes.

history.title: Pioneer 10 makes the first Jupiter flyby
history.description: Pioneer 10 became the first spacecraft to explore Jupiter, returning close-range data and images after crossing the asteroid belt.

history.title: Venera 9 returns the first image from another planet's surface
history.description: The Soviet Venera 9 lander transmitted the first photograph from the surface of another planet after touching down on Venus.

history.title: Svetlana Savitskaya becomes the first woman to spacewalk
history.description: Savitskaya left Salyut 7 with Vladimir Dzhanibekov for a 3-hour, 35-minute spacewalk that tested cutting and welding tools.

history.title: Voyager 2 makes the first Uranus flyby
history.description: Voyager 2 became the first spacecraft to visit Uranus, discovering new moons and rings while measuring the planet and its magnetic environment.

history.title: Voyager 2 makes the first Neptune flyby
history.description: Voyager 2 became the first spacecraft to visit Neptune, completing humanity's initial reconnaissance of all four giant planets.

history.title: COBE launches to map the early universe
history.description: NASA's Cosmic Background Explorer began the measurements that established the cosmic microwave background's near-perfect blackbody spectrum and mapped its tiny variations.

history.title: Galileo enters orbit around Jupiter
history.description: Galileo became the first spacecraft to orbit Jupiter while its atmospheric probe made the first direct measurements inside the giant planet.

history.title: Mars Pathfinder lands with the Sojourner rover
history.description: Pathfinder demonstrated an airbag landing on Mars and delivered Sojourner, the first rover to operate on another planet.

history.title: Chandra X-ray Observatory launches
history.description: NASA's flagship X-ray observatory launched aboard Columbia on STS-93 to study high-energy regions of the universe.

history.title: Zhai Zhigang performs China's first spacewalk
history.description: During Shenzhou 7, Zhai Zhigang completed China's first extravehicular activity, making China the third country to master independent spacewalk operations.

history.title: Kepler launches to survey worlds around other stars
history.description: NASA's Kepler space telescope began a mission that revealed planets are common throughout the Milky Way.

history.title: Dragon becomes the first commercial spacecraft berthed to the ISS
history.description: The International Space Station crew captured and berthed SpaceX's Dragon, the first commercially developed spacecraft to reach the orbital laboratory.

history.title: Voyager 1 enters interstellar space
history.description: Voyager 1 crossed the heliopause and became the first human-made object to measure the interstellar environment directly.

history.title: India's Mars Orbiter Mission reaches Mars
history.description: ISRO placed Mangalyaan into Mars orbit on its first attempt, completing India's first interplanetary mission.

history.title: Falcon Heavy makes its first flight
history.description: SpaceX's Falcon Heavy reached orbit on its demonstration mission and recovered two of its three first-stage cores.

history.title: Astronomers reveal the first image of a black hole
history.description: The Event Horizon Telescope collaboration unveiled the first direct visual evidence of a black hole and its shadow in galaxy M87.

history.title: Christina Koch and Jessica Meir complete the first all-woman spacewalk
history.description: The NASA astronauts worked outside the International Space Station for 7 hours and 17 minutes during the first spacewalk conducted only by women.

history.title: Chang'e 5 returns lunar samples to Earth
history.description: China's Chang'e 5 capsule returned 1,731 grams of lunar material, the first Moon sample return mission since 1976.

history.title: Hope becomes the first Arab mission to reach Mars
history.description: The United Arab Emirates' Hope probe entered Mars orbit, making the UAE the first Arab nation to reach another planet.

history.title: Parker Solar Probe enters the Sun's corona
history.description: Parker Solar Probe crossed the Alfvén critical surface and directly sampled particles and magnetic fields in the solar atmosphere for the first time.

history.title: Inspiration4 becomes the first all-civilian orbital spaceflight
history.description: Four private citizens launched aboard Crew Dragon Resilience on the first orbital mission crewed entirely by people who were not professional astronauts.

history.title: Polaris Dawn completes the first commercial spacewalk
history.description: The Polaris Dawn crew depressurized Dragon and tested SpaceX extravehicular suits during the first privately operated spacewalk.
